text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementHealthWhat’s All That Coffee Doing to Your Gut?Don’t worry, it’s goodJCBy Jake Currie4:00 PM CST on November 11, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleIt’s a real blessing that coffee is mostly good for us. This unique cocktail of bioactive compounds is an extremely popular beverage, and its health benefits range from mood-boosting to reducing mortality. (Of course, even if it were bad for our health, we’d probably drink it daily anyway.) Still, we don’t know that much about what habitual coffee drinking actually does to the gut. Powered By 109.5K 00ShareNextStayAnd so, to find out, a team of nutritional scientists from the University of Copenhagen sent an electronic pill on a fantastic voyage through the digestive system of both coffee lovers and infrequent coffee drinkers. On its journey, the SmartPill® was busy measuring the temperature, pH levels, and intestinal contractions. The researchers also analyzed urine and stool samples from the participants, both to get a better measure of their coffee intake and to analyze their gut flora. Read more: “How Coffee Affects Your Sex Hormone Levels”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
